about.title: About Wake County Public School System
about.content: WCPSS uses several instructional calendars, including traditional, year-round, modified, and specialized school calendars. Each MySchoolDates page identifies the calendar type it covers; families should confirm their school's assigned calendar on the official WCPSS calendar page.

districtFaqs.q: Does WCPSS use year-round and other school calendars?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. WCPSS publishes separate traditional, year-round, modified, and specialized calendars. Their start dates, breaks, and final days may differ, so confirm the calendar assigned to your school before using districtwide dates for travel or childcare planning.

districtFaqs.q: Why does WCPSS start school before Labor Day?
districtFaqs.a: North Carolina law generally allows traditional-calendar schools to open no earlier than the Monday closest to August 26. In 2026, that date is Monday, August 24, so WCPSS's August 24 start falls within the state's standard calendar window.

districtFaqs.q: How are snow days or emergency school closings handled in Wake County?
districtFaqs.a: For 2026–27, WCPSS identifies October 12, February 15, and April 5 as teacher workdays that may be used for weather makeup. When this page was reviewed on August 9, 2026, the WCPSS calendar listed six banked days and five remote instruction days. District leadership determines how weather-makeup options are used after a closure.

districtFaqs.q: What are teacher workdays and how do they affect the school calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Teacher workdays are staff planning or professional-development days when students do not attend. Some WCPSS teacher workdays can be converted to student days for weather makeup, so families should watch for district calendar updates after closures.
